rounds.text: Arham Technologies Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line compounding, delivering a 5-year compounded sales growth of 35% alongside a 5-year compounded profit growth of 29% [E14, E17]. The company's profitability and capital efficiency metrics comfortably outpace sector benchmarks, featuring an ROE of 18.8% against a sector benchmark of 9.52%, and an ROCE of 19.8% versus the sector's 11.99% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the business is conservatively financed with a manageable debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x, supported by borrowings that decreased to Rs 26 Cr in Mar 2026 [E33, E34]. Momentum is additionally underpinned by a strong Consumer Durables sector tailwind scoring +0.72, where the company's growth rates significantly exceed sector medians [E60, E61, E62]. Conceded: [E30], [E40], [E48].

While the bull highlights strong historical compounding with a 5-year sales growth of 35% and profit growth of 29% [E14, E17], these past metrics mask severe recent deterioration, evidenced by a sharp net profit drop of 33% YoY and decelerating earnings growth [E55, E56]. The claim of superior profitability and capital efficiency [E9, E10] ignores the reality of an inconsistent operating margin trend [E27, E28] and a brutal quarterly margin compression of 9 percentage points down to 10% in Mar 2026 [E26]. Conceded: [E9, E10, E14, E17]. Furthermore, the conservative financing narrative [E33, E34] collapses under the weight of an alarming cash generation crisis, where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -26 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -50 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30, E31], representing a catastrophic cash conversion ratio of -3.71x [E29]. Finally, this rich valuation is compounded by high debtors of 155 days [E49] and a significant insider exit, with promoter holding having dropped by nearly 17 percentage points since Mar 2023 [E36].
